text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedes are more than ever in debt, with outstanding debts totalling some 64 billion crowns. The inability to repay debts has more than doubled during the last five years, study shows.
Collection agents are only able to collect one ninth of the bad debt for unpaid taxes and other bills.
- Higher wages helped the Swedish economy grow in 1996, Sweden's commerce research institute (HUI) says.
- The government is planning to raise taxes on alcohol by two percent and on tobacco by nine percent.
- Prime Minister Goran Persson criticised Astra director Hakan Mogren for his outspokeness against the government in a recent speech to U.S. businessmen.
- Breweries are disappointed by new budget proposals, saying the tax cuts in beer are too low to help the industry.

- Accounting expert Olov Olson, asked by parliament's accountants to review reports done for the government by the National Audit Bureau, says the government does not provide tax payers with enough information about state finances.
- Groups of real estate owners are banding together to pressure lenders into giving them better interest rates.
